name: rusty-crew-agent-messaging
description: List same-service Rusty Crew agents, send TTL-bound internal messages, and wait for durable correlated replies. Use when an unmanaged Codex CLI session needs to communicate with a Crew agent, or when a Crew-managed Codex session should use its native rusty_crew coordination tools.
---

# Rusty Crew Agent Messaging

Choose the path before acting:

- If `rusty_crew.list_agents`, `rusty_crew.send_agent_message`, or
  `rusty_crew.agent_round` is available, use those native managed-session tools.
  Do not shell out. They are scoped to the current Crew service.
- Otherwise use the fixed production CLI below.
- Use the separately named debug CLI only when the user explicitly asks to
  communicate with debug agents. Never add an endpoint or debug switch to the
  production command.

## Managed Codex

1. Call `rusty_crew.list_agents` with no arguments.
2. Select an entry whose `routable` state is true and use its exact recipient
   ID.
3. Use `rusty_crew.send_agent_message` for one-way delivery.
4. Use `rusty_crew.agent_round` when the current turn must wait for one reply.

For send, provide `recipient` and `body`; add `correlationId` only when joining
an existing flow. For a round, provide `recipient` and `body`; optionally add
`timeoutMs` or `correlationId`. Let the tool handle JSON shape, persistence,
polling, and reply matching.

## Production CLI

Run from any shell by entering the repository explicitly:

```bash
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination -- list
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination -- send <agent-id> <ttl-seconds> <message...>
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination -- round <agent-id> <ttl-seconds> <message...>
```

List first; do not guess an agent ID. TTL is required, uses whole seconds, and
must be from 1 through 300. Prefer 30 seconds for ordinary messages and 60-120
seconds for work that may require tools.

## Debug CLI

Debug communication is deliberately off the production path:

```bash
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination:debug -- list
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination:debug -- send <agent-id> <ttl-seconds> <message...>
cd /home/dev/rusty-crew && npm run agent:coordination:debug -- round <agent-id> <ttl-seconds> <message...>
```

Do not substitute this command into a normal production workflow. The debug
client reads only `/home/system/rusty-crew-debug/config/service.env`; the
production client reads only `/home/system/rusty-crew/config/service.env`.

## Interpret Results

- `accepted`: the message was durably accepted; this is not proof of a reply.
- `replied`: the correlated round completed. Read `round.outcome.body`.
- `pending`: the round remains live; the CLI normally continues polling.
- `expired`: TTL elapsed. Treat it as terminal.
- `rejected`, `failed`, or `cancelled`: report `terminalReason` or the nested
  reason code; do not claim delivery succeeded.

Output also identifies `deploymentRole`, `targetAgentId`, `deliveryId`, and
`roundId`. Preserve these IDs when reporting or diagnosing a request.

Expired or terminal messages never resurrect. Do not retry automatically after
expiry or failure. A retry must be an explicit new message requested by the
user, with a new durable identity.
